chunks: This was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who rejected the signs of their Lord and were destroyed for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh as they were oppressors.
ai.seo_question: How were the people of Pharaoh and previous nations destroyed for their denial of God's signs?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the pattern of divine retribution against those who reject prophetic signs, linking the destruction of Pharaoh's lineage to the broader theme of 'zulm' (oppression) as the root cause. It serves as a warning that collective punishment follows persistent denial, a concept often cited in discussions of the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering under unjust rulers. The mention of 'Al-Firawn' specifically underscores the archetypal oppressor whose arrogance led to his people's demise.
